lessons.title: Signaling drill with the cited answer
lessons.summary: Each signaling answer is written here, with the RFC, before the quiz asks it.
objectives: Match a dialog with Call-ID, CSeq, branch, and To tag
Place both kinds of ACK
Say what 487 follows

illustration.title: Interview answers, signaling
illustration.caption: The quiz repeats these rows. It does not introduce a new fact.
rows: Call-ID, then the To tag once it exists
End to end. RFC 3261 and RFC 6026.

paragraphs: Interview answer: you tie a dialog together with Call-ID, and you know the dialog exists when the To tag is present. The first INVITE has no To tag. CSeq carries the number and the method, and the ACK for that INVITE keeps the number. Cite RFC 3261 sections 8 and 12.

Interview answer: the Via branch identifies one transaction on one hop. Look for the magic cookie z9hG4bK. A response matches the request when Call-ID, CSeq, and that branch agree. Cite the Via rules in RFC 3261 and the transaction rules in section 17.

Interview answer: the ACK that follows a 200 OK is end to end. It uses its own Via branch and it is aimed at the Contact from the 200. RFC 3261 defines the split. RFC 6026 corrects transaction handling for 2xx responses to INVITE.

Interview answer: the ACK that follows a non-2xx final response, including 487, is hop by hop and reuses the INVITE branch. The previous hop consumes it. If you cannot say which ACK you mean, you are not done with the question.
Interview answer: 100 Trying means this hop has the INVITE. It is not 180 Ringing and it is not the answer. Cite RFC 3261 section 21.

Interview answer: after a successful CANCEL, the CANCEL transaction completes with 200 OK and CSeq method CANCEL, and the INVITE ends with 487 Request Terminated. The ACK for that 487 is the hop-by-hop kind. Cite RFC 3261 section 21 and section 17.

lessons.title: Media drill with the cited answer
lessons.summary: 488, 422, telephone-event, RTP, and the SRTP keying choice, each answered in the prose.
objectives: Answer 488 from RFC 3261 and RFC 3264
Keep 422 on RFC 4028
Name RTP and the two keying choices

illustration.title: Interview answers, media
illustration.caption: Say the cite with the sentence.
rows: This UA refused the session description

paragraphs: Interview answer: 488 Not Acceptable Here means this user agent cannot accept the request. For media, that is usually the offer/answer overlap: no shared codec, or another part of the SDP this UA rejects. RFC 3261 names the status. RFC 3264 is the offer/answer model. RFC 6337 is the SIP usage of that model.

Interview answer: 606 Not Acceptable means the refusal is global, not local to this UA. Retrying another user agent is not the fix 606 is telling you to try. 488 and 606 are different sentences in a ticket.

Interview answer: 422 Session Interval Too Small is RFC 4028. Read Min-SE, ACK hop by hop, and send a new INVITE with a session interval at least that large. It is not a codec failure and it is not in the RFC 3261 section 21 base list.

Interview answer: telephone-event is how RFC 4733 names telephone events, including DTMF, inside the SDP. RTP, RFC 3550, carries the voice samples. PCMU payload 0 is the static assignment in RFC 3551. SIP does not carry the samples.

sections.h: Keying is a choice you record
paragraphs: Interview answer: SRTP is RFC 3711. The keying choice on an interconnect is SDES, RFC 4568, or DTLS-SRTP, RFC 5764. You record which one the two sides actually use. This lesson does not crown one of them as universal.

Interview answer: if the call connects and stays silent, the signaling may be fine and the RTP is missing. Read c= and m= from the answer, then look for packets. A keying mismatch can look like silence. Name the keying RFC you intended before you rewrite the dial plan.

lessons.title: SBC drill with the cited answer
lessons.summary: B2BUA, where PSTN SIP lands, the trusted list, and Teams TLS, answered in the body.
objectives: Call an SBC a B2BUA with RFC 7092
Land PSTN SIP on CUBE or CUCM
Separate IOS trusted-list checks from SIP RFCs

illustration.title: Interview answers, border
illustration.caption: Product pages and RFCs stay in different sentences.

layers.name: PSTN SIP
layers.detail: Lands on CUBE or CUCM, not on UCCX

layers.name: Trusted list
layers.detail: IOS voice. CME page or SRST page.

layers.name: Teams
layers.detail: TLS 1.2 or newer, FQDN in Contact

paragraphs: Interview answer: an SBC is commonly a back-to-back user agent. RFC 7092 is the taxonomy. RFC 5853 collects requirements from SIP session border control deployments. A B2BUA is a user agent server glued to a user agent client, and it may use a new Call-ID on the outbound leg. Match each leg on its own Call-ID before you call an ACK missing.

Interview answer: you do not assume the carrier leg's Call-ID is the phone's Call-ID. Record-Route is how a proxy stays on the path. A B2BUA does not need Record-Route to be in the middle, because it terminated one dialog and opened another. Say which behavior you see in the trace.

sections.h: Where trunks land, and the list
paragraphs: Interview answer: PSTN SIP lands on CUBE or CUCM. UCCX call control is through CUCM. UCCX does not terminate the carrier trunk. Cite cube-basic, cucm, and uccx. CVP SIP, if the design has CVP, comes from that version's guide. Cite cvp and do not recite a memorized comprehensive script.

Interview answer: the IP address trusted list is an IOS voice control, documented on the CME toll-fraud page and, separately, on the SRST trusted-IP page. It is not a SIP status code and not an RFC. The two pages do not share one list size, so you quote neither number as universal. In this lab the border snippet lists 198.51.100.30 and 192.0.2.40.

Interview answer: toward Microsoft Teams Direct Routing, TLS 1.2 or newer is required, and Contact must contain an FQDN or the INVITE draws 403. Cite the OPTIONS and certificate page and the Direct Routing SIP page. The SIP target this curriculum uses is sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com. The plan page is where the Direct Routing design is confirmed.

Interview answer: a handshake failure, name mismatch, untrusted CA, or old TLS, produces no SIP status. A 403 means SIP arrived and Contact failed the FQDN rule. Those are two answers. Do not merge them.

illustration.title: Boss method
illustration.caption: Synthetic Call-ID a84b4c76e66710@example.com. No customer log.

paragraphs: Symptom first: Alice at 203.0.113.10 connected and then heard silence. Write that before you write a cause. The ladder second: Call-ID a84b4c76e66710@example.com shows INVITE, 100, 180, 200, and the end-to-end ACK. CSeq 1 INVITE matches. Via branch z9hG4bK7766as01 matches the INVITE transaction. To tag 314159 is on the 200 and on the ACK.

One packet third: the 200 OK SDP says c=IN IP4 203.0.113.20 and m=audio 19642 RTP/AVP 0. That is the packet you are allowed to act on. One variable fourth: capture UDP 19642 on 203.0.113.20. Dial-peers, TLS, and the trusted list stay as they were in this window.

If the capture shows the RTP missing and you then change configuration, you still change one variable. A new codec in the offer is one window. A trusted-list address is another window. The method is the same four words even when the symptom is 488 or 503 instead of silence.

lessons.title: An interconnect checklist, not a config dump
lessons.summary: Record TLS, codecs including telephone-event, E.164, trusted addresses, OPTIONS, and the SRTP keying choice.
objectives: Fill the six checklist rows
Keep E.164 with the tel URI RFC
Stop before a full configuration dump

illustration.title: Interconnect checklist
illustration.caption: Each row is a decision. None of them is a full IOS build.
rows: Version and certificate name checks. Teams needs TLS 1.2 or newer.
The audio codecs you mean, plus telephone-event.
E.164, carried as RFC 3966 describes for the tel URI.
Only the addresses you intend. Lab pair on a border: 198.51.100.30 and 192.0.2.40.

paragraphs: TLS profile: write the version and how the certificate name is checked. Toward Teams, TLS 1.2 or newer is the floor from the OPTIONS troubleshooting page. Codecs: list the audio you intend, and include telephone-event from RFC 4733 when DTMF has to pass. Offer/answer is RFC 3264.

Numbering: write the numbers in E.164 form. RFC 3966 is how a tel URI carries a telephone number. This lesson does not invent an ITU URL. Trusted addresses: write the source list. On the teaching border that is 198.51.100.30 and 192.0.2.40, from the CME page, with SRST kept on its own page and no shared list size.

sections.h: OPTIONS, keying, and the line you do not cross
paragraphs: OPTIONS: record who sends it, how often the operations team expects an answer, and which 503 or timeout raises the alarm. The method is defined in RFC 3261 section 11. SRTP keying: write SDES or DTLS-SRTP, cite RFC 4568 or RFC 5764, and cite RFC 3711 for SRTP itself. One choice per interconnect.

The checklist is the deliverable. It is not a dial-peer dump, not a certificate private key, and not a campus queue map. Voice marking, if you mention it, is EF from RFC 3246 as mapped for telephony in RFC 4594, and the LAN design stays in the approved network document.

lessons.title: CUCM, a certified SBC, and Teams Direct Routing
lessons.summary: CUBE or another certified SBC can sit between CUCM and Teams. No architecture SKU is invented here.
objectives: Place a certified SBC between CUCM and Teams
Require TLS 1.2+ and an FQDN Contact
Keep the SIP target on sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com

illustration.title: The coexistence path
illustration.caption: Certified means the SBC Microsoft lists for Direct Routing. This lesson names no SKU.

layers.name: SBC
layers.detail: CUBE or another certified SBC. 203.0.113.20 in this lab.

paragraphs: CUBE, or another certified SBC, can sit between CUCM and Teams Direct Routing. Cite the Direct Routing plan and the CUBE basic SIP configuration guide. Certified means an SBC the Teams plan and Microsoft's current certification materials list. This lesson does not invent a platform SKU, a license tier, or a router model and call it the supported architecture.
CUCM at 198.51.100.30 sends the enterprise leg to the SBC at 203.0.113.20. The SBC speaks TLS to sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com. Those are two hops. Match each on its own Call-ID if the SBC is a B2BUA.

Teams requires TLS 1.2 or newer. Certificate name mismatch, an untrusted CA, and an old TLS version fail in the handshake, with no SIP status. Contact must be an FQDN, such as sbc.example.com in this lab, or the INVITE draws 403. Cite the OPTIONS troubleshooting page and the Direct Routing SIP page.

OPTIONS to sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com is the liveness signal once TLS is up. A synthetic 200 in this lesson means the peer answered. It is not a captured production packet and it does not prove a SKU. Confirm the rest of the design on the plan page.

lessons.title: When the RFC number moves
lessons.summary: SDP, ICE, STUN, and TURN moved. The RFC Editor banner beats a blog, and an uncited successor stays an open question.
objectives: Name the four moves this edition teaches
Read Obsoletes on the header
Mark a possible newer RFC this library does not cite

illustration.title: Moves this edition will say out loud
illustration.caption: Confirm each Obsoletes line on rfc-editor.org. A later banner outranks this table.

paragraphs: SDP moved from RFC 4566 to RFC 8866. ICE moved from RFC 5245 to RFC 8445. STUN moved from RFC 5389 to RFC 8489. TURN moved from RFC 5766 to RFC 8656. This library can cite 4566, 8866, 8445, 8489, and 8656. The older ICE, STUN, and TURN numbers are named here so you can read the Obsoletes line. They are not cite keys in this edition.

The header on the new RFC is where Obsoletes is printed. The old RFC's page is where Obsoleted by is printed. Copy the word that is there. A blog that still teaches RFC 4566 as the current SDP specification loses to the RFC Editor banner.

sections.h: What did not move in that sentence
paragraphs: SIP itself remains RFC 3261. RFC 6026 updates 2xx transaction handling and does not obsolete the base specification. Read Updates versus Obsoletes. Offer/answer remains RFC 3264. RTP remains RFC 3550. Those numbers are current in this library, and you still check their banners.
422 stays RFC 4028. Emergency calling stays RFC 6881, which is a BCP. Recording stays RFC 7866 and RFC 7865. A move in the SDP family is not a move in those documents.

sections.h: Uncertainty you are required to keep
paragraphs: A successor might exist that this edition does not cite. If the RFC Editor page for 8866, 8445, 8489, or 8656 shows a newer obsoleting document, that banner wins and this table is stale. This lesson does not claim these four numbers are permanent.

RFC 5411 can help you find the SIP family and can itself be older than the header you need. Publication months are not stated here. When a design record needs a date, copy it from the header on the day you looked.

lab.title: Cite the offer
lab.prompt: The first INVITE carries SDP. Which number is current in this library?
steps: Press Play.
Step until the hop named in the question.
Inspect that message and answer the check.

check.why: Then you still look at the RFC Editor banner in case a successor appeared.

fault.title: A frozen number
fault.symptom: A design freezes SDP as RFC 4566 and ICE as RFC 5245, and it says the table in class cannot be wrong even if the RFC Editor shows a newer document.
fault.log:
Design (synthetic): SDP RFC 4566 current. ICE RFC 5245 current.
Banner check refused.
choices: Cite RFC 8866 and RFC 8445, and accept a still newer banner if one exists.
Invent publication months to settle it
fault.why: This edition's current numbers are 8866 and 8445. An uncited successor on the banner still wins.
fault.cause: The class table was treated as permanent.
fault.fix: Open rfc-editor.org for those numbers. Write Obsoletes as printed. If the banner names a newer RFC, cite that and mark this lesson's table stale.
